p: For decades, economists assumed that consumers who were offered more choices would be better off, since a larger menu could only increase the odds of finding the ideal option. Yet a growing body of research suggests that abundance can be paralysing. Shoppers confronted with twenty-four varieties of jam were far less likely to buy any than those shown only six. The problem, researchers argue, is not that people dislike options but that each additional one raises the cost of deliberation and the likelihood of regret. Having chosen, a consumer can easily imagine that one of the rejected alternatives would have been superior, and that imagined loss erodes satisfaction with what was actually bought.
q: It can be inferred from the passage that the decline in satisfaction mainly results from
o: the lack of information about the products.
the mental comparison with options not taken.
the poor quality of the products finally chosen.
the high price attached to a wider selection.
e: 末句：选完后容易想象被放弃的选项更好，这种 imagined loss 侵蚀满意度。B 是同义改写。C、D、A 文中均未提及。

p: The museum's decision to return the bronzes to Nigeria was hailed by activists as a long-overdue act of justice. Critics, however, warned that the move could open the floodgates: if one institution conceded that its collection had been acquired through looting, others would face mounting pressure to empty their galleries. Such fears may be overstated. Restitution claims are typically handled case by case, and many objects have well-documented, entirely legitimate histories. What the episode does reveal is that the old assumption — that possession, once established, was beyond question — no longer holds.
q: The phrase “open the floodgates” (Line 3) most probably means
o: weaken the legal status of museums.
trigger a wave of similar demands.
e: 冒号后解释：一家承认掠夺，其他机构就会面临越来越大的压力清空展馆——即引发一连串类似要求。D 正确。

p: Proponents of a four-day working week point to trials in which output held steady while employees reported less stress. These results are encouraging, but they deserve more caution than they usually receive. Most trials have involved firms that volunteered to take part, which are likely to be those best suited to the change. Many lasted only six months, too short to tell whether gains survive once novelty fades. And they have been concentrated in office work, where output is notoriously hard to measure. None of this means the idea is wrong; it means the evidence is thinner than its champions admit.
q: The author's attitude towards the four-day week trials can best be described as
e: 作者承认结果 encouraging，但指出需更谨慎，列出三点局限，末句说并非想法错误，只是证据单薄。态度是谨慎保留 guarded。B 过度，A 相反，C 不符。

p: Cities have long tried to tame traffic by building more roads, only to find that new lanes fill up within a few years. Transport economists call this induced demand: when driving becomes cheaper in time, people drive more, take jobs farther away and move to distant suburbs. The reverse also appears to hold. When a major road is closed or narrowed, traffic does not simply pile up elsewhere; a portion of it vanishes, as people combine trips, switch to public transport or stay home. The lesson for planners is uncomfortable but clear: road capacity shapes behaviour at least as much as it serves it.
q: Which of the following is the best title for the passage?
o: The Hidden Costs of Public Transport
How Roads Create Their Own Traffic
e: 全文围绕 induced demand：修路引发更多交通，减路则交通部分消失，结论是道路容量塑造行为。D 最贴切。C 只是细节，B、A 文中未讨论。

p: The decline of local newspapers is often blamed on the internet, and with good reason: classified advertising, once their financial backbone, migrated almost entirely online. But researchers studying 'news deserts' — counties with no local paper — have found consequences that extend well beyond the industry. In such places, municipal borrowing costs tend to rise, apparently because no one is scrutinising how public money is spent. Voter turnout in local elections falls, and fewer candidates stand for office. The newspaper, it seems, served less as a business than as a piece of civic infrastructure whose value became visible only after it was gone.
q: According to the passage, the disappearance of local papers is associated with
o: a sharp increase in online advertising.
higher borrowing costs for local governments.
a rise in national election turnout.
e: 文中明确：news deserts 中 municipal borrowing costs tend to rise。B 正确。C 文中说的是地方选举投票率下降；A 是报纸衰落的原因而非后果；D 未提及。

p: When the first antibiotics appeared, physicians spoke confidently of the end of infectious disease. That confidence now looks naive. Bacteria reproduce so quickly that any drug used widely will select for the rare organisms able to survive it, and resistance genes can pass between species. Pharmaceutical companies, meanwhile, have largely abandoned the field: a new antibiotic, if it works, will be held in reserve and prescribed as little as possible, which is sound medicine but terrible business. The market, in other words, rewards precisely the opposite of what public health requires.
q: The author implies that new antibiotics are commercially unattractive because
o: bacteria quickly become resistant to them.
e: 关键句：新抗生素有效也会被保留、尽量少开——医学上合理，商业上糟糕。即合理使用限制销量，A。D 是背景，并非商业吸引力低的直接原因。

p: Experts are often worse at forecasting than they believe. In a celebrated twenty-year study, political specialists predicting events in their own fields performed barely better than chance, and those with grand, unifying theories did worst of all. The best forecasters were not those who knew the most, but those who were willing to revise their views in small increments as new evidence arrived. Consider weather forecasters, whose predictions have improved steadily for decades: they receive rapid, unambiguous feedback every day, and are thus forced to confront their errors in a way that most pundits never are.
q: Weather forecasters are mentioned to show that
o: scientific fields are easier to predict.
e: 举例后解释：他们每天获得快速、明确的反馈，被迫面对错误。说明反馈改善判断，A。

p: Supporters of nuclear power argue that it is indispensable to any serious plan to cut carbon emissions, since it supplies large amounts of electricity regardless of whether the wind blows or the sun shines. Opponents counter that new reactors have become ruinously expensive and slow to build, with recent projects in Europe and America running years late and billions over budget. Both sides have a point. The deeper question is whether the cost overruns are inherent to the technology or a product of the fact that Western countries, having built almost nothing for decades, have simply forgotten how.
q: The author suggests that the high cost of new reactors might be due to
e: 末句：超支可能是西方国家几十年几乎没建、忘了怎么建。即建造经验流失，D。

p: It has become fashionable to declare that the humanities are in crisis, and enrolment figures seem to bear this out. Yet the lament often rests on a curious premise: that the value of studying literature or history must be demonstrated in the currency of employability. Defenders who accept these terms — pointing out that philosophy graduates do well in law school — have already conceded the argument. A more honest defence would admit that the humanities may not make anyone richer, and insist that this is not the only, or even the most important, measure of a life.
q: The author regards defenders who cite employment data as
e: 作者说接受就业力这一前提的辩护者 have already conceded the argument，即方向错了。A misguided。B 过强：作者说更 honest 的辩护，暗示比较而非指责其撒谎。

p: Few inventions seem as humble as the shipping container, a steel box of standard dimensions. Yet its introduction in the 1950s transformed global trade more profoundly than most trade agreements. Before containers, loading a ship could take a week and required armies of dockworkers; pilfering was routine and insurance costly. Standardisation allowed cargo to move from truck to train to ship without being unpacked, slashing costs so dramatically that it became cheaper to manufacture goods on the other side of the world than in a nearby town. The box did not merely move goods; it reshaped where they were made.
q: It can be inferred that containerisation contributed to
e: 末两句：成本骤降，使在世界另一端生产比附近城镇更便宜，盒子重塑了生产地点。即制造业全球化，C。A、B 与原文相反。

p: Artificial-intelligence firms insist that their chatbots are merely tools, and that responsibility for their output lies with the people who use them. This position is convenient, but increasingly hard to sustain. The companies design the systems, choose the data on which they are trained and decide what safeguards to install. When a product reliably produces harmful results under ordinary use, we do not usually absolve the manufacturer on the ground that a customer pressed the button. The tool argument, in short, is less a principle than a shield.
q: By saying the argument is “less a principle than a shield”, the author means it is mainly used to
e: shield 盾牌，与前文 convenient 呼应：所谓“工具论”主要是公司推卸责任的挡箭牌。C。

p: Sleep was long regarded by scientists as a passive state, a mere absence of wakefulness. That view has collapsed. During sleep, the brain replays the day's experiences, strengthening some memories and discarding others. A network of channels flushes away metabolic waste, including proteins associated with Alzheimer's disease, at a rate far higher than during waking hours. Hormones regulating appetite and immunity are reset. Even a single night of poor sleep measurably impairs attention and mood. Far from being idle, the sleeping brain appears to be carrying out maintenance that cannot be performed while it is busy with the demands of the day.
q: The passage is mainly about
o: the effects of hormones on appetite.
e: 首句提出旧观点，随后逐条列出睡眠中大脑的主动功能。主旨为睡眠的积极功能，B。

p: Britain's railways were privatised in the 1990s on the theory that competition would drive down costs and improve service. In practice, competition proved elusive: a single train company usually holds the franchise for a given route, so passengers cannot choose between providers. Meanwhile, the separation of track ownership from train operation created costly disputes over who was to blame for delays. Fares rose faster than inflation. Recent governments have gradually brought operators back under public control, not out of ideological conviction but because the original model failed on its own terms.
q: According to the passage, one problem with the privatised system was that
o: passengers had too many companies to choose from.
separating track and trains caused conflicts.
e: 文中：轨道所有权与列车运营分离，导致关于延误责任的昂贵纠纷。D。C 相反；B 相反（票价上涨快于通胀）；A 不符。

p: The Mediterranean diet is routinely cited as one of the healthiest in the world, and observational studies show that people who follow it live longer. But such studies face a stubborn problem. People who eat plenty of olive oil, fish and vegetables also tend to be wealthier, better educated and more physically active, and each of these factors independently predicts longevity. Disentangling the effect of diet from that of lifestyle is extraordinarily difficult. The few randomised trials that exist are encouraging, but far smaller than the confident headlines would suggest.
q: The author would most likely agree that the benefits of the Mediterranean diet
e: 作者指出观察性研究难以区分饮食与生活方式的影响，随机试验虽令人鼓舞但规模远小于标题暗示。可能部分夸大，D。A 过于绝对。

p: Language shapes how we perceive the world, though less dramatically than once claimed. The strong version of the idea — that people cannot think what their language cannot express — has been largely abandoned. Subtler effects persist. Speakers of Guugu Yimithirr, an Australian language that describes space using compass directions rather than 'left' and 'right', maintain an astonishing sense of orientation, knowing at every moment which way is north. Their language does not make other ways of thinking impossible; it makes one habit of attention so constant that it becomes second nature.
q: The example of Guugu Yimithirr is used to illustrate that language
o: limits what people are able to think.
e: 末句：语言并不使其他思维方式不可能，而是让某种注意习惯持续到成为本能。A。D 是作者否定的强版本。

p: Every few years a new study announces that social media is making teenagers miserable, and every few years another finds the effect too small to matter. The disagreement is less mysterious than it seems. Average effects across millions of users may well be modest, while concealing serious harm to a vulnerable minority — girls already prone to anxiety, for instance. Treating the question as a simple yes or no has served neither parents nor policymakers. What is needed is research that asks not whether social media harms young people, but which young people, under what circumstances, and how.
q: The author's view of the existing debate is that it is
e: 作者批评把问题当作简单的是或否，主张研究“哪些人、何种情况、如何”。即辩论过于简单化，B。

p: The world's coral reefs occupy less than one per cent of the ocean floor yet support roughly a quarter of all marine species. They are also unusually sensitive to heat. When water temperatures rise even slightly above normal for several weeks, corals expel the algae that live in their tissues and supply most of their food, turning white in a process known as bleaching. Bleached coral is not dead, and can recover if temperatures fall. But as marine heatwaves grow more frequent, the intervals between them are becoming too short for reefs to rebuild.
q: According to the passage, the main threat to reefs is that
o: reefs cover too little of the ocean floor.
recovery time between heatwaves is shrinking.
e: 末句：热浪越来越频繁，间隔太短，珊瑚礁来不及恢复。D。C 与原文相反（白化后可恢复）。

p: Central banks have spent much of the past decade insisting that they are independent of politics, and that their decisions on interest rates rest purely on economic analysis. That claim has always been something of a polite fiction. Setting rates involves trade-offs — between savers and borrowers, between employment today and inflation tomorrow — that are inescapably distributional. Independence has value: it shields monetary policy from the temptation to engineer booms before elections. But it is better defended openly, as a deliberate delegation of power, than by pretending that technocrats face no political choices at all.
q: The author believes central bank independence should be justified by
o: its benefits to savers over borrowers.
the purely technical nature of monetary policy.
its role in preventing election-driven booms.
e: 作者认为“纯技术”说法是礼貌的虚构，独立性价值在于防止选前人为制造繁荣，应坦率辩护为有意的权力委托。C。B 正是作者否定的。

p: For most of history, cities were death traps: crowded, filthy and riddled with disease, they grew only because a steady stream of migrants from the countryside replaced those who perished. The turning point came in the nineteenth century, not with medical breakthroughs but with sewers and clean water. Engineers, rather than doctors, were the heroes of the story. Today, the urban penalty has been reversed in rich countries, where city dwellers typically outlive their rural counterparts — a remarkable inversion that owes more to pipes than to pills.
q: The phrase “the urban penalty” (Line 5) refers to
o: the high cost of living in cities.
the heavier death toll in cities.
e: 前文说城市曾是死亡陷阱，现在富国城市居民寿命反超农村，说明 urban penalty 指城市更高的死亡率，D。

p: Recycling is among the most popular of environmental habits, and among the most misunderstood. Much of what households dutifully sort is never recycled at all: contaminated loads are sent to landfill, and for years a large share of rich countries' plastic waste was simply shipped to Asia until China closed its doors in 2018. Some materials, such as aluminium, are recycled efficiently and profitably; most plastics are not. None of this means people should stop sorting their rubbish. It does mean that recycling is a poor substitute for the less comfortable step of buying and discarding less.
q: The author's main point is that
o: aluminium is the most valuable material.
China is responsible for plastic waste.
reducing consumption matters more than recycling.
e: 末句点题：回收不能替代少买少扔这一更不舒服的步骤。C。D 被作者明确否定。

p: Remote work, once a perk, became a necessity during the pandemic, and many employees have refused to give it up. Managers often complain that productivity suffers, but the evidence is mixed: some studies find gains in focused tasks, others losses in collaboration and mentoring. The less visible cost may fall on the young. Junior staff learn much of their trade by overhearing how experienced colleagues handle a difficult client or a tricky problem — knowledge that is rarely written down and hard to transmit over video calls. A workforce that never shares an office may be efficient today and impoverished tomorrow.
q: By “impoverished tomorrow”, the author suggests that remote work may
o: weaken the passing on of skills.
e: 前文讲年轻员工靠旁听资深同事学习隐性知识，远程难以传递。未来“贫乏”指技能传承削弱，B。D 与原文相反。

p: Lab-grown meat has been promised as a way to enjoy beef without the cow, and the environmental case is appealing: livestock occupy vast tracts of land and produce substantial greenhouse emissions. Yet the obstacles remain formidable. Cells must be nourished in sterile bioreactors with growth media that have historically been extremely expensive, and scaling up from laboratory flasks to industrial tanks has proved far harder than early investors assumed. Several prominent start-ups have cut staff or closed. The technology may yet succeed, but on a timescale measured in decades rather than the few years once advertised.
q: Which of the following is mentioned as a difficulty for lab-grown meat?
e: 文中：从实验室烧瓶扩大到工业罐比投资者设想的难得多。D。B、A 未提；C 不符（投资者曾乐观）。

p: Critics of standardised testing charge that it rewards wealth, narrows the curriculum and reduces children to scores. There is truth in each charge. Yet several American universities that dropped test requirements have recently reinstated them, having found that scores helped identify talented applicants from disadvantaged schools who might otherwise have been overlooked. Grades, essays and extracurricular activities, it turns out, are even more strongly shaped by family resources. The test is an imperfect instrument; the alternatives may simply be worse.
q: The author's attitude towards standardised testing is one of
e: 作者承认批评有道理（imperfect），但认为替代方案可能更糟。有保留的支持，B。

p: Why did the Industrial Revolution begin in Britain rather than in China, which in 1700 was at least as commercially sophisticated? One influential answer stresses prices. British wages were unusually high and coal unusually cheap, which made it profitable to replace workers with coal-powered machines. In China, where labour was cheap, the same machines would not have paid for themselves. On this account, British inventors were not uniquely brilliant; they were responding rationally to an unusual set of incentives — and their early, clumsy machines made sense only in a place where human effort was costly.
q: According to the explanation given, machines were adopted in Britain because
o: Britain had a larger market than China.
labour was expensive relative to energy.
e: 工资高、煤便宜，使用机器替代工人有利可图。即劳动力相对能源昂贵，D。B 被作者否定。

p: We tend to judge decisions by their outcomes, a habit psychologists call outcome bias. A surgeon who performs a risky but well-justified operation is praised if the patient survives and blamed if not, though the decision was identical in both cases. Poker players have a name for the error: 'resulting'. Skilled players know that a sound bet can lose and a foolish one can win, and they assess their play by the quality of their reasoning rather than the cards that happened to fall. Organisations that reward only results, by contrast, may end up encouraging reckless gambles that happen to pay off.
q: Poker players are mentioned to show that
o: good decisions may lead to bad results.
e: 例子说明好的下注可能输、坏的可能赢，应以推理质量而非结果评判。C。

p: Defenders of free trade have long acknowledged that while open markets enrich nations as a whole, they create losers as well as winners. The standard reply was that the gains were large enough for winners to compensate losers. In theory this was true; in practice, compensation rarely materialised. Factory towns hollowed out by import competition received modest retraining schemes that did little to restore lost livelihoods. The political backlash of recent years is, in part, the bill for that broken promise coming due.
q: The phrase “the bill … coming due” most probably means
o: the debts owed by factory towns.
e: 账单到期——比喻当年未兑现补偿承诺的后果如今显现为政治反弹。B。

p: Bilingual children were once thought to be at a disadvantage, confused by two systems competing in their heads. Research overturned that view, and for a time it was widely claimed that bilingualism conferred a broad cognitive advantage, sharpening attention and self-control. More recent and larger studies have struggled to replicate that advantage, and some researchers now suspect it was partly an artefact of publication bias, with positive findings more likely to be printed. The current consensus is more modest: speaking two languages does no harm, brings obvious practical and cultural benefits, and may or may not make one cleverer.
q: The passage mainly discusses
o: changing views on the effects of bilingualism.
e: 从“劣势论”到“认知优势论”再到“更温和的共识”，讲观点演变，B。D 只是细节，C 被质疑。

p: Insurance markets depend on uncertainty. Because no one knows whose house will burn down, everyone pays a modest premium into a common pool. Genetic testing threatens this arrangement. If insurers could see an applicant's DNA, those with high-risk genes might be priced out entirely; if applicants know their results but insurers do not, the low-risk may decline to buy cover, leaving a pool of increasingly costly customers. Many countries have banned insurers from using genetic data, but such bans address only half the problem, since they do nothing to stop individuals from acting on what they know.
q: Why does the author say the bans address “only half the problem”?
o: Insurers can still obtain DNA illegally.
They do not stop applicants from using their own results.
Many countries have refused to adopt them.
e: 末句：禁令无法阻止个人根据自己知道的结果行事（低风险者不买保险）。B。

p: The great libraries of antiquity are often imagined to have perished in a single catastrophe, the burning of Alexandria being the classic image. The reality was usually duller and more instructive. Papyrus decays; scrolls had to be recopied every few generations, and texts that no one valued enough to copy simply vanished. What survived was what successive generations chose, again and again, to preserve. The lesson has an uncomfortable modern relevance. Digital files are even more fragile than papyrus, and formats become unreadable within decades unless someone deliberately keeps them alive.
q: The author mentions digital files to suggest that
o: knowledge survives only through active preservation.
fire remains the greatest danger to records.
modern libraries are safer than ancient ones.
e: 古籍幸存靠一代代选择抄写，数字文件更脆弱，需有人刻意保存。主动保存才能延续，A。

p: Each new generation of electric vehicles is greeted with predictions that petrol cars are finished. The forecasts may eventually prove right, but the path is likely to be bumpier than enthusiasts expect. Charging networks remain patchy outside wealthy cities; batteries depend on minerals mined in a handful of countries; and governments that subsidised early buyers are quietly withdrawing support. Sales have slowed in several markets. None of this alters the long-term direction of travel. It suggests only that the transition will be decided less by technology than by the unglamorous work of infrastructure and policy.
q: The author's attitude towards the electric-vehicle transition is
e: 作者认为长期方向不变，但道路会比热衷者预期更坎坷，取决于基础设施和政策。冷静现实，A。B 过度。
